options.text: A type of cell division that produces two genetically identical cells
The process of DNA replication only
A type of cell division that produces four genetically different cells

questions.explanation: Mitosis is a type of cell division that produces two daughter cells that are genetically identical to the parent cell and to each other. Each daughter cell has the same number of chromosomes.

questions.stem: During which phase of mitosis do chromosomes line up along the middle of the cell?
questions.explanation: During metaphase, chromosomes line up along the equator (middle) of the cell, attached to spindle fibres at their centromeres.

options.text: Sister chromatids are pulled apart to opposite poles of the cell

questions.explanation: During anaphase, the centromeres split and the sister chromatids are pulled apart to opposite poles of the cell by the shortening spindle fibres.

questions.stem: Why is mitosis important for growth?

options.text: It reduces the number of chromosomes by half
It produces sex cells for reproduction
It increases the number of cells while keeping the chromosome number the same

questions.explanation: Mitosis produces new cells with the same number of chromosomes as the parent cell, allowing organisms to grow by increasing cell number while maintaining genetic consistency.

questions.stem: What must happen before mitosis can begin?

options.text: The cell wall must be removed
The cell must shrink in size

questions.explanation: Before mitosis, the cell's DNA must be replicated during the S phase of interphase, so that each daughter cell receives a complete copy of the genetic information.

questions.stem: In which phase do two new nuclei form?
questions.explanation: During telophase, the chromosomes reach the opposite poles, new nuclear envelopes form around each set of chromosomes, and two new nuclei are established.

options.text: The division of the cytoplasm to form two separate cells

questions.explanation: Cytokinesis is the final stage where the cytoplasm divides to produce two separate daughter cells. In animal cells this occurs by constriction; in plant cells a cell plate forms.
